title: From CAT to Day One: weekend mentoring in three stages
summary: Wrote CAT and waiting for your MBA to start? Eight weekends of basics, eight of case competitions and two on live projects, so you walk into class ready.
body:
*For students who have written CAT and have not started their MBA yet. About 3 minutes to read.*

The **gap between CAT and Day One** is the six or seven months after the exam and before the first class.

Most of us spend it waiting: for results, for calls, for the final list. Then we walk into a class where one person is a chartered accountant, another has five years in consulting, and someone else is an engineer who has never read a balance sheet. The case on the first day assumes everyone can do all of it.

This mentoring uses that gap. It runs on weekends only, in small cohorts, and it has three stages.

## The three stages

| Stage | Weekends | Dates (2027) | You leave with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Basics: Day Zero | 8 | 9 January to 28 February | A structured way to open any problem, the three financial statements, a simple Excel model and an industry one-pager |
| 2. Case competitions | 8 | 6 March to 25 April | A team pitch in a mock final, a ten-slide deck and written judge feedback |
| 3. Live projects brief | 2 | 1 to 9 May | A one-page project charter for a real small business, signed by its owner |

1. **Basics:** the five things every MBA class assumes you know: structuring a problem, guesstimates, accounts, Excel and reading an industry. Each week has a "starting fresh" lane and an "already know this" lane, so a commerce graduate and an engineer can sit in the same cohort. e.g. in week 2 we size how many cups of tea Indians drink in a day, out loud, in two minutes.
2. **Case competitions:** teams of three solve eight made-up practice cases, including a 24-hour sprint, then pitch to judges. This prepares you for the first-term competitions, which are where seniors and recruiters first notice a student.
3. **Live projects:** you find a real business, such as a family shop, a local café or an NGO, and agree one question with its owner. Free tools only, so there is nothing to buy.

## How it runs

- **One live session each weekend:** 90 minutes, online, in a cohort of 5 or 6.
- **One-on-one feedback:** a 30-minute call with each student every second weekend, plus written feedback on every assignment.
- **About 6 hours a week:** the session, two to three hours of reading and two to three hours on the assignment.
- **Everything in one place:** the guides, workbooks and practice cases are in the Scholar's Vault, behind a student login.

## Fees

| | Regular | Cohort 1 founding price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stage 1, Basics | ₹7,999 | ₹4,999 |
| Stage 2, Case competitions | ₹7,999 | ₹4,999 |
| Stage 3, Live projects brief | ₹1,499 on its own | Free with stages 1 and 2 |
| All three stages | ₹13,999 | ₹8,999 |

The founding price is for the first cohort only, in exchange for honest written feedback at the end.

**Offer came late?** A second Day Zero cohort starts on 15 May 2027 and finishes by 4 July, before most programmes begin.

## What this is not

This is not interview or WAT-PI coaching, and it does not promise a call, a convert or a placement. Coaching centres already do the interview part well. Here we focus on one thing: making sure you are not the person in the room who is behind on Day One.

## How to join

Seats are limited to 5 in Day Zero and 6 in the case competition cohort. To ask for a seat, or for a free 30-minute call to see which lane suits you, message Mathew directly.
